title: Gibeon: Where the Sun Stood Still: The Discovery of the Biblical City
author: James B. Pritchard
allowedUseNotes: Copyrighted excavation synthesis. Project stores its own summary of the identification evidence only; no reproductions of photographs, drawings, or inscribed-handle transcriptions.
summary: Pritchard's synthesis of his University of Pennsylvania Museum excavations at el-Jib (Tell el-Jib), 1956-1962, reporting the site's Iron Age pool and rock-cut water-tunnel system and the jar handles recovered there inscribed with the Hebrew triliteral gb'n ('Gibeon'), first published individually in his 1959 monograph 'Hebrew Inscriptions and Stamps from Gibeon.' The inscribed handles are the epigraphic basis for identifying el-Jib with biblical Gibeon, including the pool referenced in 2 Samuel 2:13. On dating: secondary summaries of Pritchard's own excavation-era conclusion describe the pool as first cut near the start of the Iron Age (Iron I), well before the pool's fill accumulated the Iron II material (8th-6th century BCE artifacts) that documents its later, much longer reuse history — see tamburrini-2021-pool-of-gibeon-3d for a more specific modern reassessment (10th century BCE construction) reaching the same construction-predates-or-is-contemporary-with-2-Samuel-2 conclusion.
confidenceNotes: Bibliographic details (title, publisher, year, handle count) assembled from secondary/tertiary summaries (Wikipedia 'Al Jib jar handles' and 'Pool of Gibeon' articles; Penn Museum Expedition Magazine pieces), not from direct inspection of Pritchard's original monographs.
